content_addressing_defect_found_and_fixe.found: The tensor store uses 64-hex filenames that LOOK like content addresses and are not. Across 12 randomly sampled tensors, ZERO have a filename equal to the sha256 of their contents, and none match the sha256 of the payload after the header, of the scales, of the codes, of the bf16 source as f32, or of the bf16 source raw. The manifest records no sha256, hash or digest field for any tensor.
content_addressing_defect_found_and_fixe.why_it_matters: G105's verify says 'rebuild from recipe, compare digests'. There were no digests to compare. G096's verify assumes content-addressed inputs. A substituted or corrupted tensor would not have been detected by name.
content_addressing_defect_found_and_fixe.fixed_forward: This seal now records a real sha256 for all 755 tensor files and a rolling digest over them, so a future rebuild has an anchor to compare against. That does NOT make the existing artifact reproducible -- it makes it VERIFIABLE from here on.

byte_reproducibility_NOT_met.why: Reproducing the NR half from the raw parent needs the ENCODER's exact rounding rule and its fusion recipe, and neither is recorded in the artifact. The manifest declares fused_in_proj_layers, so some tensors (in_proj_ba) do not exist in the parent at all and are derived -- the recipe for that derivation is not written down anywhere in the artifact.
